checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: The final video lasts five seconds.
must.why: The clip is 5 s long, with frames sampled up to 4.8 s.

must.item: Opening frame and subsequent footage match the first five seconds of the original clip.
must.why: The composition, boat pose, ripples, trees and mist closely match the original. It is an AI re-render, so the detail is softer and the framing is slightly different.

must.item: The paper boat moves at the original speed, with no retiming or reordered footage.
must.why: The boat moves about 23 px/s in both clips, and its progress through the frame is the same.

must.item: The ending is a simple cut, with no added fade or replacement shot.
must.why: The last frame at 4.8 s is a normal shot of the same scene, with no fade.

must.item: The video remains 16:9, silent and free of text.
must.why: The frame is 832×512, about 1.625:1, so it is not 16:9. The assistant disclosed this. No text is visible, and silence cannot be checked from frames.

faults.what: The aspect ratio changed from 16:9 (854×480) to 832×512, which breaks the widescreen requirement. The assistant disclosed it.
The re-render is softer and lower in quality than the original, and the boat's folds and the ripples differ slightly.
The re-render was used instead of an exact cut, so it is not a true trim.

summary: The 5-second re-render closely follows the original footage and speed with no fade, but it is 832×512 rather than 16:9 and slightly softer.
